background_notes.fact: For each finite n, Rn(n) is second countable in its Euclidean metric. The max metric on Rn(n)×ℝ induces the product topology, is second countable, and its Borel sigma algebra equals the product of the factor Borel sigma algebras.

grounds.reason: Rn(n) is the real finite-coordinate Euclidean metric space, including the one-point case n=0.
The ambient product uses the max metric and its Borel measurable structure.
S001 explicitly uses rational-coordinate boxes and the countable rectangle base to establish these ambient conditions.

background_notes.justification: For n>0, boxes with rational endpoints are a countable family and form a Euclidean base: each point of an open ball lies in such a box whose coordinate widths are sufficiently small that the sum of squared coordinate displacements stays below the squared radius. For n=0 the singleton is a base. The real line has a rational-interval countable base. A max-metric ball is a product of factor balls, so the max topology is the product topology and products of factor base elements give a countable base. Every product-open set is therefore a countable union of measurable base rectangles. Conversely, inverse images of factor Borel sets under the continuous coordinate projections are Borel. These two inclusions give the stated equality of sigma algebras.
